answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation company blog post dated 2026-07-01 (party statement, category T6). The Sharon AI CEO quote and the Firmus co-CEO quote are relayed within NVIDIA's post; the Firmus 360 MW / 170,000 GPU figures are attributed to NVIDIA's description, not to an independent filing.
answer.note: NVIDIA's own statement says it is introducing a business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, backed by a revenue-sharing and credit-support structure. Under this structure NVIDIA would earn both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity, which NVIDIA describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. Read conditionally, this points to NVIDIA moving part of its economics from one-time hardware sales toward revenue shares on AI cloud capacity, with credit support as the mechanism that lets capital-constrained AI clouds buy the hardware. The claim is a forward-looking description of a model and a partnership direction; the source gives no revenue share rate, credit-support size, participating-partner count, or dollar expectation, so it does not establish magnitude or timing of any NVIDIA revenue. The Firmus campus (expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs) and the DSX AI factory build-outs are described as plans or in-progress builds; they are supply-side and demand-side signals for NVIDIA's accelerator volume, but the source gives no completion dates, financing status or contract values for them.
limitations: The source does not disclose the revenue-share percentage, the scope of the credit support, or how much credit NVIDIA would extend, so the economic size of the model cannot be estimated from this record.

The source does not say whether any AI cloud has signed an agreement under the model; the named partners (Sharon AI, Firmus) are described as building or collaborating, and no signing status is given.

The Firmus Batam scale figures (360 MW, up to 170,000 GPUs) carry no completion date, financing status or stated share that NVIDIA would supply, so they are a plan of unknown timing rather than confirmed capacity.
The named AI natives (Baseten, Fireworks AI, Together AI) are described as demand sources for AI cloud capacity; the source does not say they purchase from NVIDIA or from these AI clouds directly.
No historical records were supplied for comparison, so this note cannot judge whether the model is new relative to prior NVIDIA financing or cloud arrangements.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's next quarterly and annual filings for any disclosure of revenue from cloud-service revenue shares, credit-support or guarantee obligations to AI clouds, and any resulting contingent liabilities.
Search for signed agreements or press releases from Sharon AI and Firmus that state contract terms, financing sources, and expected capacity-online dates for the Batam campus.
Look for any NVIDIA executive commentary on the number of AI cloud partners and the expected contribution of the model to revenue, and compare it with later filings.
